data_origin: Own finite-population method-validation audit for a binary scientific screen. The supplied census is a known reference panel used to calibrate errors, not an unknown-prevalence discovery dataset. Each recorded order is a fixed possible first16 observations from a separate uniformly randomized permutation of the complete40-unit panel. The two streams reset the panel and are separate illustrative audits. They are controlled constructed records, not empirical measurements from a named material or organism. All probability and power calculations below concern the stipulated uniform-without-replacement law over possible orders, not uniform probability on distinct binary count paths.
source_audit: Recover the actual census IDs, positive/negative memberships, population count and observed binary streams by joining each recorded unit ID to its source label. Preserve draw order, verify no repeated unit within a stream, and do not mistake multiple recorded streams for a larger population. Retain source-identified one-sided enrichment reports for BOTH labels at EVERY observed prefix using the catalog's documented hypergeometric capability, with the actual universe, membership and selected IDs. These reusable reports are needed to audit count and tail orientation; a final list of p values detached from source IDs does not complete that audit. The full16-record sequences are prerecorded for offline evaluation, so later records can explain what a deployed rule would have done after its first stopping time; an actual deployment would stop at its first rejection.
probability_model: The population size isN=40. WriteK for its total number of positive units. The null is the SINGLE finite-population hypothesisK=20, not an independent Bernoulli1/2 model or a composite one-sidedK<=20 null. The two scientific departures of interest areK=12 andK=28. In every probability calculation, draw a uniformly random order without replacement from a fixed population with that K. All binary prefixes up to the horizon16 have positive null probability. Some prefixes are impossible under an alternative and have alternative likelihood zero. Derive the exact ordered-prefix likelihood as a function of(t,s), retaining the finite remaining inventory; do not replace it with a binomial mass or assume all binary paths have equal probability.
mixture_rule: For each prefix, defineL12=P_K12(ordered observed prefix)/P_K20(ordered observed prefix) andL28 analogously. A fixed prespecified prior weightw in[0,1] definesE_t(w)=w*L12+(1-w)*L28, withE_0=1. The component is a whole-population alternative law, not a newly selected component at each step. The main deployed comparator usesw=1/2. Reject at the FIRST t in1..16 withE_t>=20; otherwise do not reject. Derive the exact null conditional expectation and justify the anytime error bound0.05 for every fixedw, including boundary weights. If deriving predictive kernels, update the posterior alternative mixture weight using observed history; a fixed mixture of one-step kernels does not generally reproduce a mixture of complete laws. Report expected number of drawsT_stop=min(first crossing,16), including all paths that never reject.
comparison_rules: P_REPEAT recomputes the ordinary exact fixed-time TWO-SIDED p valuep_t=min(1,2*min(P_K20[S_t>=s],P_K20[S_t<=s])) at eacht, and rejects at the firstp_t<=0.05. The lower tail can be checked as the right tail for the negative label in the same finite panel. MAX_LR instead rejects at the firstmax(L12,L28)>=20. Neither rule is to be conflated with the fixed-prior mixture. Assess actual finite-horizon errors underK20 and powers underK12,K28, separately from whether a rule has the stated martingale justification. A lack of that generic proof is not itself evidence that its actual error in this specific finite experiment exceeds0.05. Conversely, a valid fixed-time p value need not remain level0.05 under repeated checking. For MAX_LR also compute its null expectation after the FIRST draw and compare it with its initial value1.
full_law_certification: For all three fixed comparator rules, derive exact rejection probabilities and expected draws underK12,20,28 over the complete random-order law. Retain a reproducible first-hit probability recurrence or complete weighted enumeration; probabilities of terminal counts alone do not determine an event that depends on an earlier crossing. Check total rejected-plus-surviving probability conservation. A Monte Carlo frequency is not the requested exact calibration. Distinguish an anytime upper bound, the actual finite-horizon false-positive rate, and power.
continuous_prior_design: Within the fixed-priorE_t(w)>=20 family only, maximize the WORST of the two exact horizon16 rejection probabilities underK12 andK28. Find the COMPLETE set of globally optimalw values, not just one plausible symmetric choice or a numerical weight grid. The stopping event changes only at finitely many criticalw values where one reachable(t,s) hasE_t(w)=20. Derive this finite arrangement and inspect every open cell AND every critical point, retaining the inclusive crossing convention at equality. Certify the best worst-case power and all endpoint inclusions. Return the midpoint of the complete optimal interval as one preselected deployment weight, but say whether that weight is the unique optimum. Every such fixed-prior process must still meet its null anytime guarantee; do not tune the weight on the actual observed stream and then reuse the fixed-weight proof.
questions: Produce the full source-based prefix enrichment audit, then compute both recorded streams' fixed-time two-sided p values andw=1/2 mixture e values at all16 prefixes. Identify each comparator's first crossing, and explain why the last e value alone can fail to reveal an earlier valid stopping decision.

Derive and calibrate all three stopping rules against the complete finite-population laws, including exact power and expected sampling cost. Establish the fixed-mixture martingale proof, the first-step MAX_LR expectation, and which comparison actually violates the nominal5percent error in this declared finite experiment.

Solve the continuous fixed-prior minimax-power design globally, including every equality boundary and the complete optimal set. Keep its pre-data guarantee distinct from a post hoc choice of the best-looking alternative.
reporting: null_population_total; null_positive_count; observed_binary_streams mapsS1,S2 to16 integers; prefix_diagnostics_by_stream mapsS1,S2 to{two_sided_fixed_time_p,mixture_e_value,mixture_first_crossing,repeated_p_first_crossing,maxLR_first_crossing}, where each probability/e-value field is a16-number array and crossings are integer ornull; null_rejection_probability_and_expected_draws_by_rule mapsMIX_HALF,P_REPEAT,MAX_LR to[probability,expected_draws]; alternative_power_and_expected_draws mapsK12,K28 to objects with the same rule keys and pair values; optimal_weight_interval; optimal_interval_endpoints_included as two booleans; optimal_worst_alternative_power; midpoint_optimal_deployment_weight; optimal_weight_is_unique asboolean; maxLR_null_first_step_expectation; maxLR_has_unadjusted_martingale_justification asboolean; final_e_value_alone_can_miss_prior_crossing asboolean; valid_interpretation_proposal_ids. Counts,crossings,booleans,IDs exact. Numerical absolute tolerance1e-8. Full probability recurrences, null guarantees, source-linked tail reports and complete critical-weight certificates belong in the trajectory.

interpretation_proposals.A: Ordered sampling without replacement has history-dependent remaining inventories, so an independent-binomial likelihood is a different model.
interpretation_proposals.B: Every rule using exact5percent fixed-time p values automatically has a5percent error after arbitrary repeated checking.
interpretation_proposals.C: A fixed mixture of complete alternative likelihood ratios is a null martingale, even though its posterior mixture weights change after observing data.
interpretation_proposals.D: Taking the larger of two likelihood ratios automatically preserves the original unit-mean martingale proof without a multiplicity cost.
interpretation_proposals.E: A stopping decision can be validly triggered before an e process later falls below its threshold.
interpretation_proposals.F: A method lacking the generic mixture proof must have actual false-positive probability above5percent in every finite experiment.
interpretation_proposals.G: A global prior-weight design must inspect isolated equality points as well as open cells, because the stopping threshold is inclusive.
interpretation_proposals.H: One optimal symmetric weight proves that the global optimizing weight is unique.
interpretation_proposals.I: Exact finite-horizon calibration can be more conservative than a valid anytime bound, and this difference should be reported rather than erased.
